question.problem:
Consider the inhomogeneous system  ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)+g(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution $x(t)$ passing through $x({t}_{0})$ is presented below.

$\text{L1}:\,$ Let $y(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)$  

$\text{L2}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)=-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}{x}^{′}(t)$  

$\text{L3}:\,$ ${y}^{′}(t)={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t)$  

$\text{L4}:\,$ $y(t)-y({t}_{0})={\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L5}:\,$ $y({t}_{0})=x({t}_{0})$ 

$\text{L6}:\,$ $y(t)=x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{-A(s-{t}_{0})}g(s)\,\text{d}s$  

$\text{L7}:\,$ ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

$\text{L8}:\,$ ${e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t)=x(t)$

$\text{L9}:\,$ $x(t)={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}x({t}_{0})+{\int }_{{t}_{0}}^{t}{e}^{A(t-s)}g(s)\,\text{d}s$

Select the correct options to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\,$ Line $\text{L4}$ follows from $\text{L3}$ by  
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L5}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by  
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Line $\text{L8}$ follows from line $\text{L1}$ by  
{{field-3}}.

current_example.problem:
Consider the inhomogeneous system  $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t),$ where $A$ is a constant square matrix. A derivation of the formula for the solution $\mathbf{x}(t)$ passing through $\mathbf{x}(t_0)$ is presented below.

$\textrm{L1}{:}\;$ Let $\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t)$  

$\textrm{L2}{:}\;$ $\mathbf{y}'(t) = -Ae^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t) + e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}'(t)$  

$\textrm{L3}{:}\;$ $\mathbf{y}'(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{g}(t)$  

$\textrm{L4}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{y}(t)-\mathbf{y}(t_0) = \int_{t_0}^{t} e^{-A(s-t_0)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$

$\textrm{L5}{:}\;$ $\mathbf{y}(t_0)=\mathbf{x}(t_0)$ 

$\textrm{L6}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{y}(t)=\mathbf{x}(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{-A(s-t_0)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$  

$\textrm{L7}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{A(t-s)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$

$\textrm{L8}{:}\;$ $e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{y}(t)=\mathbf{x}(t)$

$\textrm{L9}{:}\;$ $\displaystyle\mathbf{x}(t)=e^{A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t_0)+\int_{t_0}^{t} e^{A(t-s)}\mathbf{g}(s) \, \text{d}s$

Fill in the blanks with the correct reasons to justify each step of the reasoning.

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L3}$ follows from $\textrm{L2}$ by  ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/6217024e2cdc96b661fba2cc6bfa10d672731a36fd2161eafcfb898a53cbca84.svg).

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L5}$ follows from line $\textrm{L1}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/0fbeabf9ff2d98a4091913f2d01d46505ad891e9d938ae736860192d280347f7.svg).

$\quad$ Line $\textrm{L8}$ follows from line $\textrm{L1}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/c13adbf58868e249b48bbd4d767831f95d8e3cff938f272bb040ab7d764e3be5.svg).
current_example.worked_solution:
Let's justify each of the selected steps.

- We first consider lines $\textrm{L2}$ and $\textrm{L3}.$ Starting from

$$
\mathbf{y}'(t) = -Ae^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t) + e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}'(t)
$$

in $\textrm{L2}$ and substituting $\mathbf{x}'(t)=A\mathbf{x}(t)+\mathbf{g}(t)$ from the original system gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′}(t) & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}(Ax(t)+g(t)) \\  & =-A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+A{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t)+{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t) \\  & ={e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}g(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $\textrm{L3}$ follows from $\textrm{L2}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/3a929d5c04a9933b606727579384a7f08fb85e1a4ef1be7c5caaa2aa3a30288a.svg)

- Next, we consider lines $\textrm{L1}$ and $\textrm{L5}.$ Evaluating $\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t)$ at $t=t_0$ gives

$$
\mathbf{y}(t_0)=e^{-A(t_0-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t_0)=I\mathbf{x}(t_0)=\mathbf{x}(t_0).
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{L5}$ follows from line $\textrm{L1}$  by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/1705e418ad373005ab9674b6939aa9ee9cbc0e9d5f9326981668dea65aae0e2d.svg)

- Finally, we consider lines $\textrm{L1}$ and $\textrm{L8}.$ Multiplying both sides of

$$
\mathbf{y}(t)=e^{-A(t-t_0)}\mathbf{x}(t)
$$

from $\textrm{L1}$ by $e^{A(t-t_0)}$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}y(t) & ={e}^{A(t-{t}_{0})}{e}^{-A(t-{t}_{0})}x(t) \\  & =x(t).\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $\textrm{L8}$ follows from $\textrm{L1}$ by ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14155694/assets/d925fd1c14f534263ffafc1a0af56c0a1ef1d171371540ed62ecadd865f8202f.svg)
